title: podman compose errors on network aliases override
body:
### Issue Description

```
/tmp [1]> cat repro.yml 
services:
  test:
    image: alpine
    networks: !override
      dev:
        aliases: [test]

networks:
  dev: {}
/tmp> podman compose -f repro.yml config
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/bin/podman-compose", line 6, in <module>
    sys.exit(main())
             ~~~~^^
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 4969, in main
    asyncio.run(async_main())
    ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/asyncio/runners.py", line 205, in run
    return runner.run(main)
           ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/asyncio/runners.py", line 128, in run
    return self._loop.run_until_complete(task)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/asyncio/base_events.py", line 719, in run_until_complete
    return future.result()
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 4964, in async_main
    await podman_compose.run()
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 2370, in run
    self._parse_compose_file()
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 2591, in _parse_compose_file
    content = load_yaml_or_die(filename, f)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 2201, in load_yaml_or_die
    return yaml.safe_load(stream)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/__init__.py", line 125, in safe_load
    return load(stream, SafeLoader)
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/__init__.py", line 81, in load
    return loader.get_single_data()
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 51, in get_single_data
    return self.construct_document(node)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 60, in construct_document
    for dummy in generator:
                 ^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 413, in construct_yaml_map
    value = self.construct_mapping(node)
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 218, in construct_mapping
    return super().construct_mapping(node, deep=deep)
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 143, in construct_mapping
    value = self.construct_object(value_node, deep=deep)
  File "/usr/lib64/python3.14/site-packages/yaml/constructor.py", line 100, in construct_object
    data = constructor(self, node)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 1709, in from_yaml
    return OverrideTag(node.value)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.14/site-packages/podman_compose.py", line 1701, in __init__
    self.value[item[0].value] = [i.value for i in item[1].value]  # type: ignore[index]
                                 ^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'value'
Error: executing podman-compose -f repro.yml config: exit status 1
```

```
/tmp> rpm -q podman

/tmp> cat /etc/os-release

```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Make a file repro.yml with the contents shown above
2. Try to run podman compose -f repro.yml config with podman compose provider set to podman-compose
3. Observe stacktrace


### Describe the results you received

An error about the config

### Describe the results you expected

The config should be loaded correctly. I'm not sure how much compatibility is kept with docker compose but this feels simple enough that podman compose should support it.

comments.body:
podman-compose issues must be reported there https://github.com/containers/podman-compose/

We (podman) do not support podman-compose or docker-compose directly
